fixes.explanation: Good guess, but Paul doesn't say clouds anywhere in this verse. He says that if he speaks in the tongues of men and of angels but has not love, he is only "…a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal." Those are instruments that make a lot of sound. I think Paul wants us to hear how loud that can be without love.

Fair thought, but that's not in Paul's list. He says, "Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud." So when someone else gets the bigger blessing, the answer in the list is that love does not envy. Paul doesn't say anything here about asking for the same.

That sounds patient, and love is patient. But Paul's list goes on: "Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy…" So when someone else gets the bigger blessing, what he says love does is not envy. Patient and kind are right there in the same list with it.

You got it, baker. Paul says love "…keeps no account of wrongs." Somebody does you dirty, and love doesn't file it away for later. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I can tell you, that's one pile of old receipts love never keeps.

Not quite, friend. Paul says love "…rejoices in the truth." Its own success isn't what he names here. Just before this he says love "…does not boast…" and "…is not self-seeking…" so I think the truth is where he wants our joy to land.

Ha, that's not where Paul goes. Right before this he says love "…keeps no account of wrongs." Then he says love "…takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth." Its joy is the truth, not getting even.

That's right, friend. Paul says love "…bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things." Hopes ALL things, not just the easy ones. That's four "all things" in a row, and he means every one.

Yes, that's it. Paul says, "Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face." Now it's a dim reflection, and then it's face to face. I think that's the part worth waiting for.

Close, but a clearer mirror isn't what Paul says. He says, "Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face." The answer is face to face. That's the contrast he draws with the dim reflection.

Easy to second-guess, but it matches what Paul says. He writes, "Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known." So the statement is true. He knows in part now, and then he will know fully.
